(p-4243) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat al-Anbiya (The Prophets)

It was named thus because it contains great virtues concerning a group of the prophets, peace be upon them.

It is a Meccan surah, though some have excepted from it the verse: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 44]. It has one hundred and twelve verses. Al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Bani Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta-Ha, and al-Anbiya' are among the first of the old treasures (al-'atiq al-awwal), and they are of my ancient wealth (talidi)."

Ibn al-Athir said: That is, from the first things I took and learned in Mecca. Al-talid is the old property that was born with you, and it is the opposite of al-tarif (newly acquired property).

(p-4244) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[1] ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near for them, while they are heedless, turning away.﴾

﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near for them﴾, that is: what they were promised in the Book of the otherworldly reckoning, which is their punishment, has approached the people of Mecca. ﴿While they are heedless﴾, that is: of what is intended for them. ﴿Turning away﴾, that is: denying it. It was near because every thing that comes, however long the times of awaiting and expecting it, is near. Allah, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿Indeed they see it as far off. But We see it as near﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 6-7]. And He, may He be exalted, has said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will not fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Hajj: 47]. The eloquent warning contained in the generality of (al-nas, "the people") is not hidden. It is right that people should take heed of the nearness of the Hour, so that they may make up for their neglect through repentance and regret. Likewise, in calling the Day of Resurrection the Day of Reckoning there is an added awakening, because the reckoning is what reveals a person's state, so the title itself contains something to be feared. It is not far-fetched to say that reckoning is more general than the worldly and the otherworldly, and in that case there is an indication of the nearness of the reckoning of the idolaters of Mecca, through taking retribution from them and triumphing over them, as was indicated in the verse: ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring the victory﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 52], and He promised it to the Prophet and his companions in many verses. However, the fame of the reckoning after the otherworldly resurrection led the exegetes to restrict the verse to it. And Allah knows best. And His saying, may He be exalted:

The discussion concerning His words, Exalted is He:

[2] ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed, but they listen to it while playing.﴾

[p. 4245] ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed, but they listen to it while playing.﴾ This is a rebuke to them for opposing wisdom with its opposite, and a declaration of their manifest ignorance. For what reminds in the most complete manner and alerts to heedlessness in the most thorough manner deserves that hearts humble themselves before it and souls submit to it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: After describing them with heedlessness together with aversion, He affirmed their aversion to the one who admonishes and to the one who awakens. God renews the reminder for them from time to time, and brings them a verse after a verse and a sura after a sura, so that admonition and warning may be repeated in their ears, perhaps they will be mindful. Yet listening to the verses and suras, and the various kinds of admonitions and insights they contain, which are the truest of truths and the most serious of matters, only increases them in play, diversion, and mockery. The word "reminder" (dhikr) refers to the portion of the Qur'an sent down. End of quotation.

Note: This passage is cited by those who hold that the recited speech of God is created (hadith). They are the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), the Karramiyyah (followers of Ibn Karram), and the Ash'ariyyah (followers of al-Ash'ari). As for the Mu'tazilah, they said that the Qur'an is created only because it is composed of sounds and letters. It therefore subsists in something other than God. They said that the meaning of His being a speaker is that He creates those letters and sounds in a body, such as the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), or Gabriel, or the Prophet, peace be upon him, or others, like the tree of Moses.

As for the Karramiyyah, when they saw that what the Mu'tazilah had committed to was contrary to custom and language, they held that His speech is an attribute of His, composed of created letters and sounds that subsist in His own essence, exalted is He. They thus held that the signifier and the signified are created, and they permitted God to be a locus of contingent events.

The Ash'ariyyah said: The recited speech indicates the eternal, inner attribute, which for them is speech in its true sense.

They said: What was sent down upon the prophets of letters and sounds, which they heard and conveyed to their peoples, is created, described by change, multiplicity, and descent. It is not what it signifies, which is that eternal attribute. The question is well known, and scholars have much to say about it. The point is that the verse mentioned was taken as evidence by those who cited it for what they held.

[p. 4246] The Imam Ibn Taymiyyah, may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him, counted this argument among the errors. His words in his book (Muwafaqat al-Manqul li-l-Ma'qul, "The Agreement of Transmitted and Rational Evidence") are: Whoever says that the Qur'an, or the expression of the Qur'an, is created argues with this verse, though the verse's indication is more against their view than for it. For it indicates that some of the reminder is newly revealed and some of it is not newly revealed, and this is the opposite of their view. Furthermore, "newly revealed" (muhdath) in the general usage of the Arabic language is not what it is in the technical usage of the people of kalam (speculative theology). For the Arabs call whatever has just come into being "new" (hadith), and what preceded others "old" (qadim), even if it was non-existent before, as in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Like the old withered palm-stalk﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:39), and His words concerning the brothers of Joseph: ﴿Indeed, you are in your old error﴾ (Yusuf 12:95), and His words: ﴿And since they were not guided by it, they will say, "This is an old lie."﴾ (al-Ahqaf 46:11), and His words concerning Abraham: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping,﴾ (al-Shu'ara 26:75) ﴿you and your forefathers of old?﴾ (al-Shu'ara 26:76). End of quotation.

The gnostic Ibn 'Arabi said in the three hundred and sixty-ninth chapter of his Futuhat (Meccan Openings) concerning this verse: The meaning is that its coming is newly arrived, not that its essence is newly created. Its knowledge became new for them when they heard it. This is like when you say: "A guest has newly arrived for us today," while it is known that he existed before he came. Likewise the Qur'an came in new matters to which hearing was attached, but understanding did not attach itself to what the words indicated. So it is new from one aspect and eternal from another. End of quotation.

If you say: The speech belongs to God, and the rendering belongs to the speaker, then the answer is yes. This is so, by the evidence of His words, swearing an oath: ﴿Indeed, it is the speech of a noble messenger﴾ (al-Haqqah 69:40), meaning the Qur'an. He attributed the speech to the intermediary and the translator, just as He attributed it to Himself, saying: ﴿Then grant him protection until he hears the words of God﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:6). When the Qur'an is recited to us, we have heard the speech of God, Exalted is He. When Moses was addressed by his Lord, he heard the speech of God. But between the two kinds of hearers lies the distance of the two easts. For what one who hears the speech of God without intermediary perceives is not equal to what one who hears it through intermediaries perceives. End of quotation.

As for the doctrine, the position transmitted from the people of the Sunnah and the community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, the adherents of the prophetic tradition and the consensus of the Muslims), the imams of hadith and the early generations (al-salaf), as Ibn Taymiyyah stated in (Minhaj al-Sunnah, "The Path of the Sunnah"), is that God, Exalted is He, has never descended speaking whenever He wills with a speech that subsists in Him. He speaks with an audible voice. The species of speech is eternal, even if the particular voice is not itself eternal.

In other words, He, Exalted is He, has never ceased to be characterized by speech. He speaks by His will and power, one thing after another. Thus His speech is contingent in its individual instances and eternal in its kind.

Then he, may God have mercy on him, said: If it is said to us: You have affirmed that contingent events subsist in the Lord, we say: Yes. This is our position, which is indicated by revelation and reason. Whoever does not say that the Creator speaks, wills, loves, hates, is pleased, comes, and arrives has contradicted the Book of God. Whoever says that He has always been calling Moses in eternity has contradicted the speech of God while also rejecting reason. For God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿When he came to it, he was called﴾ (al-Naml 27:8), and He says: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:82). Here He uses letters that indicate the future.

Then he, may God have mercy on him, said: They said, meaning the imams of the people of hadith and others among the companions of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and others: In sum, everything the Mu'tazilah and the Shi'ah cite that indicates that His speech is connected to His will and power, and that He speaks when He wills and speaks one thing after another, we affirm. Whatever those who say that the speech of God subsists in His essence, and that it is an attribute of His, and that an attribute subsists only in the thing described, we also affirm. We have taken what is correct in the statement of each of the two groups, and we have departed from what revelation and reason reject in the statement of each of them. If they say to us: This necessitates that contingent events subsist in Him, we say: And who (p. 4248) among those before you, from the early generations and imams, denied this? The texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah include this, together with clear reason. It is a doctrine necessarily entailed for all the groups, and whoever denies it has not recognized its necessary implications and what they entail. The term "contingent events" (hawadith) is ambiguous; it may refer to accidents and deficiencies, and God is exalted above that. Rather, there subsists in Him what He wills and is able to do of His speech, His acts, and the like, which is indicated by the Book and the Sunnah.

Then he said: The view that He is always speaking and always acting by His will is transmitted from the early generations and the imams of the Muslims, from the People of the House and others, such as Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Bukhari, Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, and others.

Then he said: We affirm what agrees with reason and transmission regarding the perfection of His power and will: that He is able to act by Himself however He wills. We say He has always been characterized by the attributes of perfection, speaking in His essence. So we do not say that His speech is created and separate from Him, for the reality of this view is that He does not speak. Nor do we say that it is one thing, command, prohibition, and report together, for this is rejecting reason. Nor do we say that it is discrete, opposing, eternal sounds, for sounds do not remain for two moments. Moreover, if we said this and the previous view, it would follow that God's speaking to the angels, to Moses, and to His creatures on the Day of Resurrection is nothing but the creation of perception in them. Then what was eternal would not have been eternal, while it is known that the texts indicate the opposite of that. Nor do we say that He became a speaker after He was not one, for that would be describing Him with perfection after deficiency, even if He became a locus of contingent events by which He became perfect after His deficiency. Moreover, the occurrence of that perfection necessarily has a cause, and what is said about the second is like what is said about the first. Thus in it is the renewal of His majesty and the continuity of His acts. End of the abridged quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 3:

Then Allah Most High explained what they were conspiring about in their misguidance, by His saying, glorified is He:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Most High:

[3] ﴿Their hearts are heedless. And they conceal their private counsel, those who did wrong: "Is this not but a human being like you? Will you then submit to magic while you see?"﴾

﴿Their hearts are heedless. And they conceal their private counsel, those who did wrong: "Is this not but a human being like you?"﴾ That is: they concealed this discourse in order to turn people away from the way of Allah. The phrase "alladhina" (those who) is either a substitute (badal) for the waw of "asarru" (they conceal), or a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is "asarru", or it is in the accusative of censure (mansub 'ala al-dhamm). ﴿Will you then submit to magic﴾ That is: will you yield to it and follow it? His saying, "while you see," is a circumstantial clause (hal) emphasizing the denunciation and the disbelief. Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: They believed that the Messenger of Allah could only be an angel, and that everyone among humans who claimed prophethood and brought a miracle was a sorcerer, and his miracle was his sorcery. Therefore they said, by way of denunciation: "Will you then attend to magic while you witness and observe that it is magic?"

Abu al-Su'ud said: And he overlooked that the sending of a human to all of mankind is what wisdom in legislation requires. And His saying, Most High:

[4] "He said: My Lord knows every word in the heaven and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

"He said, 'My Lord'" is a narration of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them. It is also read as "Say" (qul), in the imperative addressed to him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him: "He knows the word in the heaven and the earth" and "He is the All-Hearing" meaning, of what they concealed, "the All-Knowing" meaning, with knowledge of it, so He will requite them.

The commentary, having shown their confusion over the various forms of incoherence, and that they did not confine themselves to what was previously mentioned of the claim of sorcery, explains this with His words:

**The discussion on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, words:**

[5] ﴿Nay, they say: "A medley of dreams! Nay, he has invented it! Nay, he is a poet! Let him bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent with signs."﴾

﴿Nay, they say: a medley of dreams﴾, i.e., confused jumbles that he sees in sleep. ﴿Nay, he has invented it﴾, i.e., he has fabricated it. ﴿Nay, he is a poet﴾, i.e., what he brought is poetry that conjures for people meanings that have no reality. Such is the way of the refuted falsifier: he never ceases to shift between falsehood and what is more false, and to waver between corruption and what is more corrupt. ﴿Let him bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent﴾, i.e., a sign like the sign with which the earlier ones were sent, meaning: so that we may believe in him. Then, exalted is He, pointed out their lying in claiming belief upon the arrival of a sign, just as He points to their demand for it, with His words, glorified and exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 6:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[6] ﴿Not before them did any town that We destroyed believe. So will they believe?﴾

﴿Not before them did any town that We destroyed believe. So will they believe?﴾ That is: no nation of the destroyed peoples believed when the signs they proposed were granted. Will these people believe if they are answered in what they asked and given what they proposed, while they are more stubborn and more rebellious than those? And in this there is an alert that withholding the sign proposed was for the sake of sparing them, for if it came and they did not believe, they would deserve the punishment of annihilation, as those before them did. We have already noted that the advancement of the human species in the prophetic era required that the sign be rational (ʿaqliyyah), not cosmic (kawniyyah). So reflect on this.

Then he clarified the answer to their doubt concerning the incompatibility of humanity with messengership, by His saying, may He be exalted:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And We sent not before you any but men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know.﴾

﴿And We sent not before you any but men to whom We revealed﴾: that is, not angels. It is also read with the yā' (yūḥī, "to whom We reveal") and with a fatḥa on the ḥā' (i.e., the verb is read in the passive, "to whom it is revealed," with the form read with a fatḥa). ﴿So ask the people of the reminder﴾: that is, the scholars of the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿If you do not know﴾: that is, that the messengers were human beings, so they will inform you that the messengers were not angels. In the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of seeking support from the statements of the People of the Book and their narrations, for the purpose of confronting the opponent and persuading him.

Caution:

Al-Razi said: As for what many jurists have attached to this verse, regarding the layman's right to refer to the fatwas of the scholars, and the mujtahid's right to follow the view of another mujtahid, it is far-fetched. This is because this verse is a direct address spoken face to face, it was revealed concerning this particular occurrence, and it is specifically connected to the Jews and Christians. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 8:

Then Exalted God explained that the Messengers were like other people in the matters pertaining to human nature, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of the words of God Exalted:

[8] ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.﴾

﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾ meaning: bodies that are free of need for food, but rather in need of that in order to compensate for what is lost through metabolism (tahlil), as God Exalted said: ﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ [al-Furqan: 20]. In this divine description of the state of the Messenger lies the greatest deterrent against those who withdraw from people, who hunt the hearts of the common folk, the masses, the foolish, and those who do not weigh a gnat's wing in the sight of their Lord. For they regard eating food at gatherings, increasing the number of people in assemblies, and going out to the markets to attend to needs, as among the greatest destroyers of the edifices of belief in them. Thus you see them disdaining to buy their own needs with their own hands, though that is the Sunnah; and [disdaining] walking in the markets, though that is permissible; and [disdaining] accepting an invitation, though it is obligatory, due to delusions they have built up within themselves; and out of concern for reputation they guard its flank. (p-4252) Woe to them, a people of innovators who worship the hearts of creation and do not worship God, and who desire a state above that of the Messengers of God. Yet that is only for God. How bold they are in contending with the Almighty! And how patient they are in facing the Fire!

As for His saying, Exalted: ﴿nor were they immortal﴾, meaning: in this world; rather they lived and then died, as God Exalted said: ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you﴾ [al-Anbiya: 34]. Their distinguishing feature is that they receive revelation from God, Mighty and Majestic; angels descend upon them with what He decrees in His creation of what He commands and forbids. Their being human is part of the completeness of the divine blessing, for it enables the one to whom the Messenger is sent to take from them and benefit from them, since kind is more inclined toward kind.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.﴾

﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ means: in their triumph over their enemies, as in ﴿God has decreed: "Surely I shall prevail, I and My messengers"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21]. ﴿And We saved them and whom We willed﴾ means: from among their followers, and those whom wisdom decreed should be preserved. ﴿And We destroyed the transgressors﴾ means: those who exceeded the bounds in disbelief. Then, exalted is He, drew attention to the nobility of the Qur'an, urging them to recognize its worth, by His saying:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[10] ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance. Will you not then understand?﴾

﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance﴾: meaning, your honour and your renown, by which you are remembered, is above the honour of all other nobles. ﴿Will you not then understand?﴾: meaning, will you not appreciate this blessing and receive it with acceptance? As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44]. It has also been said that the meaning of "your remembrance" is "your admonition," so that "remembrance" in the sense of "reminding" is in the genitive of the object. Abu al-Su'ud said: "This is the most fitting interpretation with the context and the flow of this noble arrangement, for His, the Exalted, words ﴿Will you not then understand?﴾ are a reproachful rebuke, containing an incitement for them to reflect upon the matter of the Book and to contemplate what it contains of various kinds of admonitions and warnings, among which are the calamities preceding and following it." Then the Exalted indicated a kind of detail to the summary of the destruction of the transgressors mentioned before it, by His saying:

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[11] ﴿How many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and We raised up after it another people.﴾ [12] ﴿So when they perceived Our might, behold, they were fleeing from it.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 12] [13] ﴿"Do not flee, and return to what you were given to enjoy and your dwellings, that you may be questioned."﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 13].

﴿How many a town did We shatter, which had been wrongdoing, and We raised up after it another people.﴾ ﴿So when they perceived Our might﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 12], i.e., Our punishment descending upon them: ﴿behold, they were fleeing from it﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 12], i.e., they were running away in haste. Then it was said to them, mockingly, either by the tongue of circumstance or by the tongue of speech: ﴿"Do not flee, and return to what you were given to enjoy in it"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 13], i.e., of luxury and pleasure. The particle (fi, "in") here is either locative or causal. ﴿"And your dwellings"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 13], i.e., those in which their extravagance had abounded. ﴿"That you may be questioned"﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 13], i.e., that you may be sought out for consultation, deliberation, and planning in matters of importance and calamities.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[14] ﴿They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [15] ﴿And that claim of theirs did not cease until We made them as a harvest, extinguished.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 15] [16] ﴿And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 16]

(p-4254) ﴿They said﴾, i.e., when they became certain of the descent of the punishment: ﴿"Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿And that claim of theirs did not cease﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 15], i.e., that utterance, which is "Woe to us," was their constant call. It is not restricted to the time of bewilderment, but persists for as long as they were able to speak. ﴿Until We made them as a harvest﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 15], i.e., like a crop that has been reaped. ﴿Extinguished﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 15], i.e., destroyed by the quenching of the fire of their souls. ﴿And We did not create the heaven and earth and that between them in play﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 16], i.e., rather it was for bestowing favour upon them. We did not bestow this favour upon them except so that they would be thankful for it and turn to that for which they were created.

Al-Zamakhshari, may God have mercy on him, said: That is, We did not level this raised ceiling and this spread-out bed, and what is between them of kinds of creatures, filled with varieties of wonders and marvels, as tyrants level their ceilings, their beds and all their adornments, for amusement and play. Rather, We levelled them for religious benefits and divine wisdoms, so that they would be places for reflection, consideration, inference and contemplation for Our servants, along with the benefits connected to them that cannot be counted and the conveniences that cannot be enumerated.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In this verse there is a general indication that the creation of the world and the origination of the children of Adam are founded upon the principles of profound wisdoms, which lead to sublime ends. It is also an admonition that what has been related of the mighty punishment and the descending retribution upon the people of the towns is among the requirements of those wisdoms and their branches, in accordance with what their deeds necessitated. And that those addressed who follow in their footsteps have sins like their sins. That is, We did not create them, nor what is between them, in this wondrous pattern and impregnable manner, empty of wisdoms and benefits. Rather, He expressed this by "play" and "amusement," where it says "in play," to clarify the perfection of His exaltedness above creating something devoid of wisdom, by depicting it in the form of something no one doubts is impossible to proceed from Him, exalted is He. Rather, We created them and what is between them only so that they would be a beginning for the existence of man, a cause for his livelihood, and a proof leading him to attain Our knowledge, which is the ultimate goal, through obedience to Us and worship of Us. As His saying, exalted is He, attests: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Hud: 7], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56].

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 17:

And His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[17] ﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to be doing [such]﴾.

﴿Had We wished to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to be doing [such]﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) confirming what precedes it regarding the negation of play and amusement. That is: had We wished to take something with which to amuse Ourselves and play, We would have taken it from Our own presence, like the custom of the tyrants in raising lofty buildings and beautifying them, and levelling couches and adorning them. But Our wishing it is impossible, because it contradicts wisdom. Therefore Our taking it is categorically impossible. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿if We were to be doing [such]﴾, its answer (jawab) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. That is: We would have taken it. It has also been said that (in) is negative, meaning: We were not doing [such], i.e., taking up play, because of Our not wishing it. Thus it serves as an explanation for the negation of the consequent through the negation of the antecedent.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[18] ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe.﴾

﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood﴾ is a shift (*idrab*, a turning away from one matter to another) away from taking play as a pastime, or rather away from desiring it. It is a declaration of His transcendence above His exalted essence, as if He had said: "Glory be to Us that We should take play and sport, or desire it. Rather, it is within Our nature to refute falsehood with truth, so that it is crushed (*fa-yadmaghuhu*), that is, utterly annihilated, as We did to the people of the cities mentioned." ﴿Behold, it vanishes﴾ means it is utterly destroyed. The word *qadhf* (hurling), which is a forceful throwing of a solid body such as a rock, has been borrowed for sending truth against falsehood. And for its annihilation of falsehood, *dam'* (crushing), which is the breaking of a soft, hollow thing, namely the brain, in such a way that its membrane is split, leading to the departure of the soul, is a metaphor (*isti'ara*) that is explicit and dependent (*isti'ara tasrihiyya tab'iyya*). It may also be an image (*tamthil*) for the overcoming of truth over falsehood until it removes it, by hurling a solid body onto the head of a soft brain so as to split it. The phrase ﴿behold, it vanishes﴾ is mentioned to reinforce the metaphor (*tarshih al-majaz*), because whoever strikes and crushes causes the soul to depart, so it is among its necessary consequences. Abu al-Su'ud said: In the sudden *idha* (behold) and the nominal sentence there is a indication of the complete swiftness in departing and perishing, which is not hidden. It is as if it were vanishing from its very origin. (p-4256) In the verse there is an allusion to the elevation of truth and the lowliness of falsehood, and that the side of the first remains while the second perishes. ﴿And woe to you for what you describe﴾ means: for what you ascribe to Him of taking offspring and the like, from which His greatness is exalted.

Then, after informing of His dominion over all creation, God, may He be exalted, told of the servitude of the angels to Him, their constant obedience to Him night and day, and their freedom from the fabricated sonship attributed to them, with His words:

[19] ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him do not disdain His worship, nor do they tire.﴾

﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., ownership and governance. ﴿And those near Him﴾, who are the angels, ﴿do not disdain His worship, nor do they tire﴾, i.e., they do not grow weary or exhausted from it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire.﴾

﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never tire.﴾ That is: through extolling Him (tanzih) and worshipping Him,

Then He, exalted is He, pointed to affirming His oneness in divinity and negating rivals, following His affirmation of the matter of the message. For what preceded from the beginning of the surah was concerned with establishing the matter of prophethood, by His saying, glory be to Him:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾

﴿Or have they taken gods from the earth who raise the dead?﴾ That is: who resurrect the dead and bring them out from non-existence into existence.

That is, rather, they have taken gods from the earth who, despite their lowliness and inanimateness, raise the dead. No indeed, for those they have taken as gods are far removed from that. So how did they make them equal to God and worship them alongside Him?

Al-Zamakhshari, may God have mercy on him, said: If you say, how does He deny them the taking of gods that resurrect, when they did not claim this for their gods? How could they, when they are the furthest thing from this claim? For they, while acknowledging that God, mighty and majestic, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "God."﴾ [Luqman: 25], and that He is capable of all capable things and of the first creation, were deniers of resurrection. They say: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], and it was in their view among the impossibilities beyond the power of the Capable, like a second eternal being. So how would they claim it for an inanimate object that is not described with power at all?

I say: The matter is as you have mentioned. However, by their claim of divinity for them, it necessarily follows that they must claim for them the power of resurrection. For the name does not deserve to be applied except to one capable of every capable thing, and resurrection is among the capable things. End of quote.

Al-Intisaf said: Thus the denial directed at them is of the explicit claim and its necessary implication, and this is more emphatic in denial.

Then al-Zamakhshari said: In it is a kind of mockery of them, rebuke, and denunciation of their ignorance, and an indication that what they deemed far-fetched from God is not to be deemed far-fetched, for when divinity is valid, the power to originate and to restore is valid along with it. End of quote.

A subtle point:

The secret of His saying, from the earth, is belittlement, that is, belittling the idols by describing them as earthly and lowly. It has also been permitted that it denotes specification, that is: the gods that are of the kind of the earth, because they are either carved from some stones or made from some of the earth's substances. He specified the denial to them because what is earthly and made by their own hands, how can it claim divinity?

[Page 4258]

Then, Exalted is He, He demonstrated the invalidity of multiplying gods by establishing proof not merely of their non-existence but of their impossibility, through His saying, glorified is He:

[p-4258] The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined. So glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾

﴿Had there been in them﴾, i.e., exercising authority over the heavens and the earth, ﴿gods other than Allah﴾, i.e., besides Him, ﴿both would have been ruined﴾, i.e., both would have been voided along with everything in them, and their observable order would have been disrupted, as He, exalted is He, said in Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿And there was not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have gone off with what he created, and some of them would have overcome others﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91]. Abu al-Su'ud said: Since the consequent is negated, the antecedent is definitively negated. The demonstration of the necessary implication (mulazama): divinity necessitates the capacity to exercise absolute independent control over the two, in change and alteration, in origination and annihilation, in giving life and causing death. So their remaining as they are is either through the influence of each of them, which is impossible because it is impossible for a specific effect to occur from multiple causes; or through the influence of only one of them, in which case the rest are definitively outside divinity. Know that making the consequent their corruption after their existence is because the antecedent considered the plurality of gods within them. Otherwise, the proof necessitates the impossibility of plurality absolutely, for if the god were plural, then if all agree on the purpose, their powers would compete over it, and if they disagree, they would obstruct one another; so nothing would exist at all. And since the consequent is negated, the antecedent is necessarily negated. End.

Its detail, as in (al-Maqasid): if two gods existed with the attributes of divinity, and one of them willed a matter, such as the motion of a body for example, then either the other is able to will its opposite or not. Both are impossible. As for the first, because if it is supposed that his will relates to that opposite, then either their purpose occurs, which is impossible because it implies the joining of opposites; or the purpose of neither occurs, which is impossible because it implies the incapacity of the two gods described with perfect power, given the supposition, and because it implies the elimination of the two opposites, whose non-occupation of the locus is impossible, such as the motion and rest of a body at a specific time. Or the purpose of one of them occurs without the other, which is impossible, because it implies preference without a preponderant cause, and the incapacity of the one supposed to be capable since his purpose did not occur. This proof is called the proof of mutual obstruction (burhan al-tamana'). To it refers His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined﴾. If by corruption is meant the non-occurrence of existence (al-takawwun), then its formulation is that if the god were plural, the heavens and the earth would not have come into being, because their coming into being is either by the combined two powers, or by each of them, or by one of them. All are invalid. As for the first, because it is part of the nature of a god to have perfect power. As for the other two, because of what has passed. And if by corruption is meant departure from the order in which they are, then its formulation is that if the god were plural, there would be conflict and domination between them, and the work of each would be distinguished from the work of the other by the necessity of custom. Thus that harmony among the parts of the world would not have been achieved, by which the whole becomes like a single person, and the order by which the species persist and effects follow would be disrupted. End.

This being so, it has been said: the matter here is a demonstrative proof (burhani), while what is referred to in the verse is persuasive (iqna'i). It does not produce certain knowledge, so it is not valid to argue with it for this matter. Among those who elaborated this is al-Taftazani in (Sharh al-'Aqa'id al-Nasafiyya), criticizing what he himself indicated in (Sharh al-Maqasid) regarding the verse being a proof, as we mentioned from him. The summary of his speech is that mere plurality does not necessarily entail actual corruption, because agreement on this order is possible, i.e., by partnership or by one of them delegating to the other. So plurality does not necessitate actual mutual obstruction, but only possible obstruction. Possibility does not necessitate occurrence, so it is permissible that no such obstruction occurs between them, but rather that they agree on bringing them into being. It was refuted by saying that the possibility of obstruction necessitates actual obstruction in every created thing through the way of independently willing its origination. And whenever obstruction is necessitated, no created thing comes into existence at all. For if it existed under the aforementioned obstruction necessitated by plurality, then either by the combined two powers, which entails their incapacity; or by each of them, which entails interference; or by one of them, which entails preponderance without a preponderant cause, since the relation of every possible thing to the power of each of the two gods is equal, and all of these are necessarily impossible. The conclusion of the argument is that if the gods were plural, no created thing would come into being, because plurality necessitates the possibility of disagreement, which necessitates either interference or incapacity. Thus it is clear that the verse is a decisive proof, since the necessary implication in it is decisive. Some of them verified the decisiveness of the necessary implication by the habitual custom which, never once in history, has been found to be violated: that two powerful kings in one city each seek sole rule and superiority over the other and to subdue him. How then could two gods, while God is described with the utmost degree of majesty, not seek sole sovereignty, as He, glorified is He, has informed us by His saying: ﴿and some of them would have overcome others﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91]? When this is considered, the soul scarcely brings its contrary to mind, let alone supposes it, while being certain that the actual state is the other. [p-4260] Upon this supposition, then, the implication is certain knowledge. This is the summary of what came in refuting the view of al-Sa'd in the glosses (al-Hawashi). Numerous people criticized his earlier view severely, and his contemporary 'Abd al-Latif al-Karmani exaggerated in his criticism.

The scholar al-Marjani said: Abu al-Mu'in al-Nasafi preceded him in this in his book (al-Tabsira), and the author of (al-Kashf) followed him, where he severely criticized Abu Hashim al-Jubba'i, to the point of attributing to him disbelief for his casting doubt on the verse's definitive indication of this claim. It is not hidden that understandings do not stop at a limit; they continue to differ and conflict as forms and colors differ, and there is no takfir nor declaring astray, so long as a person remains upon the right path.

The Mufti of Egypt clarified the explanation of this implication in the treatise (al-Tawhid) with a clarity beyond which nothing more is possible, and his words are: Among what is necessary for Him, exalted is He, is the attribute of oneness, in essence, attribute, existence, and action. As for essential oneness, we have established it previously by negating composition in His essence, externally and mentally. As for oneness in attribute, i.e., that no existent equals Him in His attributes that are established for Him, this is due to what we have shown: that the attribute follows the level of existence, and there is nothing among existents that equals the Necessary Existent in the level of existence. So none equals Him in what follows existence of attributes. As for oneness in existence and in action, by which we mean the singularity in necessary existence and what follows from it of bringing about contingent things, this is established, because if the Necessary Existent were plural, each of the two Necessaries would have a determination differing from the other's determination by necessity; otherwise the meaning of plurality would not be realized. And whenever determinations differ, the attributes established for the determined essences differ, because an attribute is determined and attains its specific reality only by the determination of that to which it is established by self-evidence. Thus knowledge and will differ according to the difference of the necessary essences, since each one would have a knowledge and will that are distinct from the knowledge and will of the other, and each would have a knowledge and will suited to its essence and its specific determination. This difference is essential, because the knowledge and will of the Necessary are necessarily from its essence, not from an external matter. So there is no way to change or alter them, as has preceded. We have already established that the act of the Necessary proceeds from Him only according to His knowledge and the judgment of His will, so the act of each would proceed according to a judgment that differs from the other's [p-4261] in an essential difference. If the Necessaries were plural, their acts would differ according to the difference of their knowledges and wills, a difference with which agreement is impossible. And each one, by the requirement of the necessity of its existence and what follows from it of attributes, has authority over origination in all contingent things. So each has disposal over each of them according to its knowledge and will, and there is no preponderant cause for the execution of one of the two powers over the other. Thus their actions would conflict according to the conflict in their knowledges and wills, and the order of the cosmos would be corrupted; indeed it would be impossible for it to have an order at all, and indeed impossible for any contingent thing to exist. Because every contingent thing necessarily — i.e., origination relates to it — according to the differing knowledges and wills. Then it would be necessary for one thing to have multiple existences, which is impossible. So: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined﴾. But corruption is impossible by self-evidence. He, may His majesty be great, is one in His essence and attributes, having no partner in His existence nor in His actions. End.

Al-Ghazali, the Proof of Islam, in his book (al-Iqtisad fi al-I'tiqad), in the section on oneness, pointed out that there is no clearer proof of the demonstration of monotheism than this verse, and that there is no addition beyond the explanation of the Qur'an. Al-Kalanbawi said: The corruption mentioned in this verse is either in the sense of the heavens and the earth departing from this observed order of the persistence of species and the following of effects, as is apparent; or in the sense of their not coming into being in the first place, as they have said. Then, everyone addressed by it knows that the source of corruption is the plurality of gods. So by its wording, it negates plural gods other than the Necessary, exalted is He, and by its indication, it negates the plurality of gods. End.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾, i.e., of a partner with Him in the heavens and the earth. The "fa" (so) indicates the consequence of what follows from what precedes, namely the establishment of unity through the aforementioned proof. I.e., so glorify Him, glorifying Him as is befitting to Him, and exalt Him above what they fabricate. In it is an expression of wonder at those who associate with the Supreme Worshipped One, the Originator of the greatest of created beings, which is the Throne, others who have no power over anything whatsoever.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.﴾

﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does﴾ — i.e., He is the Judge whose judgment none can reverse, and none can object to Him, owing to His greatness (ʿaẓama), His majesty (jalal), His magnificence (kibriyaʾ), His exaltedness (ʿulluw), His wisdom (ḥikma), His justice (ʿadl) and His kindness (luṭf). ﴿But they will be questioned﴾ — the pronoun refers to the servants; i.e., they will be questioned about what they do, as in His saying: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 92–93].

Al-Zamakhshari said: If it is the custom of kings and tyrants that those within their realm do not question them about their actions and about what they bring forth and issue of the management of their kingdom, out of awe and reverence, while error, slips and various kinds of corruption are permitted for them, then the King of kings and Lord of lords, their Creator and Provider, is more worthy of not being questioned about His actions, especially since it is known and established in minds that everything He does is done with wisdom, and error is not possible for Him. Then he said: ﴿But they will be questioned﴾, i.e., they are owned, enslaved and erring. How fitting it is that they be told: "Why did you do it?" concerning everything they did. End of quote.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse is like His saying: ﴿He protects, and none can protect against Him﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 88].

Note:

Imam al-Ghazali said in (al-Madnun bihi ʿala Ghayr Ahlihi): As for the meaning of God's saying, ﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾, and His saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, why have You raised me blind, when I was seeing?"﴾ [Taha: 125], the word "question" (suʾal) may be used to mean holding someone to account (ilzam). One says: so-and-so debated so-and-so and directed his question at him. It may also be used to mean inquiry (istikhbar), as a student asks his teacher. God, exalted is He, is not subject to questioning in the sense of holding to account, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿He cannot be questioned about what He does﴾, since it is not said "why?" in the sense of holding to account. As for not being inquired of or asked for information, that is not the case, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Why have You raised me blind﴾ [Taha: 125]. And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say: "Bring your proof. This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.﴾

﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him?﴾ He repeated it to magnify their disbelief and to display their ignorance, and to move on to showing the falsity of their taking gods, while those gods are devoid of the attributes of divinity, and to rebuke them by establishing proof for their claim. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Bring your proof"﴾, that is, your evidence for what you invent. As for the standpoint of reason and transmitted revelation, there is no validity to a saying for which there is no proof or evidence.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In attributing the proof to their pronoun there is an indication that they have a proof, which is a form of mockery of them. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me﴾ is an illumination of His proof and an indication that it is something to which all the divine books bore witness, and to which the tongues of all the earlier messengers testified. It is also an increase in stirring them up to establish a proof, so as to display the completeness of their incapacity. That is: this revelation that has come concerning monotheism, containing the decisive rational proof, is a reminder for my community, that is, their admonition, and a reminder for the earlier nations. I have established it, so you too establish your proof. End of quote.

Then He, exalted is He, indicated that argument does not benefit them, in establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away﴾, that is, from the reflection that leads to guidance.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that tawhid (affirming the oneness of God) is the call of every prophet, by His saying:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him﴾. It is also read as yūḥā (with the yā' and a fatḥah on the ḥā'), and the rest is: ﴿that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾. This is as He said: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint deities other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 45]. And He said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid taghut (every object of worship other than Allah)"﴾ [an-Nahl: 36]. So every prophet whom Allah sent called to the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him. The natural disposition (fitrah) also bears witness to this. As for the polytheists, they have no proof, and their argument is void with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.

Then Allah, exalted is He, demonstrated the falsehood of what some of the polytheists invent, that the angels are His daughters, exalted is He far above that, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.﴾ [27] ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 26–27]

﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.﴾ That is: brought near [to Him] (muqarrabun).

﴿They do not precede Him in speech﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 27] That is: they follow His word, so they do not say anything until He speaks it or commands them to say it, as is the way of disciplined servants. ﴿And they act by His command﴾: they do not disobey Him in any matter. This is an indication of their observance of the etiquette of servanthood in actions as well as in words.

﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants.﴾ That is: brought near [to Him] (muqarrabun).

﴿They do not precede Him in speech﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 27] That is: they follow His word, so they do not say anything until He speaks it or commands them to say it, as is the way of disciplined servants. ﴿And they act by His command﴾: they do not disobey Him in any matter. The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive.﴾

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ means: of what they have put forward and what they have left behind. So He is the One who encompasses them in knowledge: ﴿and they encompass nothing of His knowledge﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. How, then, could they step outside His servitude? ﴿And they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾ means: that He should intercede for him, out of awe of Him, exalted is He.

Al-Mahayimi said: How could they step outside His servitude when they cannot even attempt the least form of opposing Him? For they do not intercede (p-4265) except for one whom He approves, since intercession for one He does not approve is a kind of opposition to Him. And how could they oppose Him? ﴿And they are, out of His fear﴾, that is, of His subjugation: ﴿apprehensive﴾, that is, fearful.

Ibn Kathir said: His saying ﴿and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and His saying: ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba': 23], and in many other verses with the same meaning.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[29] ﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ The pronoun in (minhum, "among them") refers to the angels, because they were mentioned earlier, the context calls for it, and it is more forceful in refutation and threat.

Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: After He had described their honour with Him and the nearness of their station to Him, praised them, and attributed to them those noble deeds and pleasing works, He suddenly issued a severe warning and threatened with the punishment of Hell whoever among them would associate [a partner with Him]. This is on the basis of supposition and illustration, while His knowledge encompasses that it will not happen, as He said: ﴿Had they associated [others with Allah], what they used to do would have been worthless to them﴾ [al-An'am: 88]. By this He intended to make the matter of association (shirk) appear monstrous and to magnify the standing of monotheism (tawhid). End of quotation.

In His saying ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ there is an indication that whoever utters such a monstrous claim is a wrongdoer. How could it not be so, when he has treated the rank of divinity with contempt and overstepped with it its exalted station?

(p-4266) Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[30] ﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? And We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?﴾

﴿Have not those who disbelieved considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? And We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?﴾

This begins the discussion of His cosmic signs, which point to His oneness in divinity, and which the polytheists were blind to, so they did not look at them with the sight of reflection and contemplation. The meaning of His saying ﴿were a joined entity﴾ is: they did not send down rain nor cause plants to grow. ﴿And We separated them﴾ means: by the rain and the plants. Thus "splitting" (fatq) and "joining" (ratq) are metaphors. Similar to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿By the sky with its return﴾ [al-Tariq: 11] ﴿and the earth with its cracking open﴾ [al-Tariq: 12]. Linguistically, "al-raj'" (return) is water, and "al-sad'" (cracking) is plants, because it cracks the earth, that is, splits it open. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then let man look at his food﴾ [Abasa: 24], meaning how We uniquely brought it into being and prepared it so that it would sustain its structure: ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾ [Abasa: 25], meaning from the clouds, after it had not been; ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾ [Abasa: 26], meaning: after the earth had been a joined mass with its parts tightly bound, We split it in a visible, observable split, as you see in the earth after irrigation, or a splitting by plants.

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: It is permissible that by "splitting" is meant bringing into existence and manifesting, as in His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 11], and His saying: ﴿He said: Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them﴾ [al-Anbiya: 56]. Thus He reports bringing into existence with the word "splitting" and the state before bringing into existence with the word "joining."

al-Razi said: The verification of this is that non-existence is pure negation, so there are in it no distinct essences or separate entities, but rather it is as one connected, similar thing. When realities come into existence, then at the moment of existence and creation some of them separate from others and some are detached from others. This approach is good: it makes "joining" a metaphor for non-existence and "splitting" a metaphor for existence. End.

Some astronomers said: The meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿were a joined entity﴾ is: one single thing.

The meaning of: ﴿And We separated them﴾ is: We separated some of them from others.

He said: The verse indicates that the earth was created like the rest of the wandering planets in every respect, i.e., that it is one of these wandering bodies, similar to them in substance, in the manner of creation, in its circling around the sun and drawing light and heat from it, in being inhabited by living creatures like the other planets, and in being spherical in shape. Thus the planets, or the heavens, are alike in every respect, all created from one substance, which is the substance of the sun, and in one manner. End of his words.

The first interpretation of the verse may be preferred, because of His saying after it: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾, for this shows that what precedes it is connected to water. On this view, the seeing in His saying ﴿Have they not seen﴾ is visual. On the view of Abu Muslim and what follows it, it is cognitive, in the same way as His saying to His Prophet, may the blessings of God be upon him: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephant?﴾ [al-Fil: 1], although he did not witness the event, having been born after it, and he knew it only through true reports. Likewise the splitting and joining here, in their last two senses, are among what God, Exalted is He, reported through the tongue of one whose truthfulness and infallibility are established by proof, so it was easy for them to affirm it, and so it was known.

The meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ is: We made every living thing, by means of water, unable to live without it. This includes plants and trees, for from water they become growing things, and moisture, greenness, blossoms and fruit come to be in them. Attributing life to the appearance of plants is well known in many verses, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He brings the earth to life after its death﴾ [al-Rum: 19]. Some restricted "every thing" to animals, relying on the verse: ﴿And God created every creature from water﴾ [al-Nur: 45], but there is no necessity for this. Rather, generality is more indicative of power, greater in lesson, more eloquent in address, and more subtle in meaning.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Will they not then believe?﴾ is a rebuke for their failure to believe in God, Exalted is He, alone, despite the manifest signs that necessarily require it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 31:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[31] ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We placed in it broad roads as pathways, that they may be guided.﴾

﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾ i.e., fixed mountains. ﴿Lest it should shake with them﴾ i.e., lest it move and be agitated with them. Were it not for the mountains, the earth would be in constant agitation because of the materials in its interior, which are perpetually in turmoil (al-jayashan).

As for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And We placed in it broad roads as pathways, that they may be guided﴾: the pronoun in (fiha) refers to the earth. The repetition of the verb is due to the difference between the two things placed, and to give the context of enumerating favours (maqam al-imtinan) its due. Or the pronoun refers to the mountains, since they are the ones in need of roads. Ibn Kathir restricted himself to the second view. He said: "A huge mountain may be seen between two lands, and in it there is a gap through which people pass, as a mercy from Him, exalted is He."

"Subulan" (pathways) is a substitute (badal) for "fijajan" (broad roads). By this it is indicated that, despite their width, they are passable and travelled, and that they were created and widened for the sake of travellers. The meaning of ﴿that they may be guided﴾ is: to their interests (ila masalihihim). And His saying, may He be exalted:

The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[32] ﴿And We made the heaven a protected canopy, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾

﴿And We made the heaven a canopy﴾ meaning: over the earth, like a dome over it. ﴿Protected﴾ meaning: elevated and guarded from being reached (p-4269), or protected from change by external influences, however long time extends. Like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We built above you seven strong ones﴾ (an-Naba': 12). ﴿Yet they turn away from its signs﴾ meaning: from what God has placed in it of proofs and lessons, in the sun, the moon, and the rest of the luminous bodies, and their courses, their rising and their setting, according to a sound reckoning and a wondrous arrangement, which indicate profound wisdom and overwhelming power. What ignorance is greater than the ignorance of one who turns away from them and whose imagination does not lead him to reflect upon them, to take lessons from them, and to infer the greatness of the One who brought them into being from non-existence, who arranged them, set them in this placement, and deposited in them what He deposited, which none knows the reality of except Him, whose power is mighty and whose knowledge is subtle?

It has been read (qira'a): ﴿ayatihā﴾ (in the singular), with the singular used as sufficient to indicate the genus, meaning: they are attentive to what comes to them from the heaven of worldly benefits, such as being illuminated by its two moons and guided by its stars, and the life of the earth and of animals by its rains. And regarding its being a clear sign pointing to the Creator, they turn away. This was related by az-Zamakhshari.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 33:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿It is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit is swimming.﴾

﴿It is He who created the night﴾, meaning: so that they may rest therein; ﴿and the day﴾, so that they may move about for their livelihood and be active in their works; ﴿and the sun and the moon﴾, meaning: as a light and as a reckoning; ﴿each in an orbit is swimming﴾, meaning: each one of them runs in the orbit (falak), like a swimmer in water. And the "falak" (orbit) in the language is everything that revolves.

Some of the scholars of astronomy (ʿulamaʾ al-falak) said: the verse points to the motion of these celestial bodies, like His saying: ﴿So I swear by the receding stars﴾ [al-Takwir: 15] ﴿that run and hide﴾ [al-Takwir: 16]. Both indicate that the motion of the stars is intrinsic (dhatiyyah), not as the ancients say, that the stars are fixed in their orbits (aflak) which carry them around, and by their rotation the stars move.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 34:

And His saying:

(p-4270) The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:

[34] ﴿We did not grant to any human before you eternity. So if you die, will they be eternal?﴾.

﴿We did not grant to any human before you eternity. So if you die, will they be eternal?﴾ It was revealed when they said: ﴿We await for him the misfortunes of time﴾ [al-Tur: 30]. They used to presume that he would die, so they would rejoice at his death, hoping for the end of the Prophetic call (da'wah) and the dispersal of its order upon the loss of the thread that strung its pearls together. So God Most High negated from him that rejoicing through this verse, by what He decreed: that He does not make any human eternal in this world, since that would contradict the cosmic wisdom (al-hikmah al-takwiniyyah). And He informed, by the preservation of His revelation and its guarding from corrupting influences for as long as the world endures, through His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

Ibn Kathir said: Those scholars who held that al-Khidr (peace be upon him) has died and is not alive until now have used this noble verse as evidence, since he is a human, whether he was a saint (wali), a prophet (nabi), or a messenger (rasul). End of quote.

The elaboration of this has already preceded in surah al-Kahf, so refer back to it. And in the meaning of the verse is the saying of 'Urwah the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him:

Whenever time drags its heavy chest over a people, it kneels down upon others of us.

So say to those who gloat over us: "Be watchful, the gloaters will meet what we have met."

And the saying of al-Shafi'i:

Some people wish that I would die, and if I die, that is a path in which I will not be the only one.

So say to the one who seeks to oppose what has passed: "Prepare yourself for another like it, as if it has already come."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 35:

(p-4271) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[35] ﴿Every soul shall taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as a trial. And to Us you will be returned.﴾

﴿Every soul shall taste death. And We test you with evil and with good﴾ meaning: We examine you with what calls for patience among calamities, and what calls for gratitude among blessings. ﴿As a trial﴾, that is, as a test. It is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing "lanabluwakum" (We will test you) without its own verb form. ﴿And to Us you will be returned﴾, meaning: We will then recompense you according to what comes forth from you of patience or gratitude.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He called that a trial (ibtila') though He is knowing of what the doers will do before their existence, because it is in the form of testing; that is, it is a metaphorical representation (isti'arah tamthiliyyah). Al-Qadi said: In the verse there is an indication that the purpose of this life is trial and exposure to reward and punishment, confirming what has preceded. He placed evil first because it is the fitting thing for those who are being denounced.

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[36] ﴿When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾

This verse refers to the mockers of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and his like, who used to scoff at his message, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and who would become enraged at the reviling of their gods and the belittling of their intellects. As the Exalted said: ﴿And when they see you, they take you only in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 41] ﴿He had almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them. But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in way.﴾ [al-Furqan: 42]

The annexation of "mention" (dhikr) to "the Most Merciful" (li-l-Rahman) is an annexation of the verbal noun to its object, i.e., "mention of His Oneness." Or it is to the subject, i.e., by His guiding the creation through the sending of messengers and the sending down of books as a mercy upon them. Or [it means] by the Qur'an. "They are disbelievers" means: they are more deserving of being mocked. The repetition of the pronoun is for emphasis and specification.

(p-4272) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿Man was created of haste. I shall show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.﴾

﴿Man was created of haste﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And man has ever been hasty﴾ [al-Isra: 11]. It is made (as if he were created from haste) because of his excessive eagerness and his lack of patience, as if he were created from it. It is like your saying: "Zayd was created from generosity," treating what he was naturally disposed to in character as if it were the elements of which he himself was made, signifying the utmost degree of its being inseparable from him and his never being detached from it. So the verse is a metaphor in the form of an implicit comparison (isti'arah makniyyah), by likening haste, in that it is innate to him, to its substance (the material from which he is made). It is also permissible that it be an explicit metaphor (isti'arah tasrihiyyah). The intended meaning of "man" is the species. Among his haste is his rushing toward disbelief and his urgent demand for the threat: ﴿I shall show you My signs﴾, that is, My retributions in this world, like the event of Badr, and in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire. ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten them﴾, that is, to bring them.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[38] ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾

﴿And they say, "When is this promise?"﴾ That is, the promise of the otherworldly punishment, said in mockery and denial, not seeking to specify its time. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in its coming.

Al-Zamakhshari said: They used to hasten the punishment of God and His signs, which compel knowledge and acknowledgment. So He intended to forbid them from hastening and to rebuke them. He first mentioned the blameworthiness of man for excessive haste and that he is created with it. Then He forbade them and rebuked them, as if He said: It is no novelty for you to be hasty, for you are inclined to that; it is your nature and disposition.

Then he explained the terror of what they are hastening for and the horror of what it contains, and that their haste is due to their ignorance of its outcome, by His saying, exalted is He:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ [40] ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, so they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:39–40].

﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs﴾, i.e., they will not be able to push it away from their most noble and strongest limbs. The mention of the face comes first because of its nobility, and also because warding it off is more important than warding off anything else. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., by anyone pushing it away from them. The answer to "law" (law) is omitted, meaning: "when they were hasty." It has also been said that "law" here expresses wishing, and has no answer. ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:40], i.e., unexpectedly, and it will confound them. For if they wish to endure it, they will not be able to; and if they wish to repel it, ﴿they will not be able to repel it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:40], i.e., by any means whatsoever. ﴿Nor will they be given respite﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:40], i.e., they will not be granted a moment's rest, since the period of reprieve before it will have been completed. Then he alluded to consoling him, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding their mockery, within a threat to them, by His saying, exalted is He:

Then he explained the terror of what they are hastening for and the horror of what it contains, and that their haste is due to their ignorance of its outcome, by His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ [40] ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, so they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite.﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:39–40].

﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs﴾, i.e., they will not be able to push it away from their most noble and strongest limbs. The mention of the face comes first because of its nobility, and also because warding it off is more important than warding off anything else. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, i.e., by anyone pushing it away from them.
