And His saying, exalted is He:

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[87] ﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger, and thought that We would not decree (any hardship) for him, then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ [88] ﴿So We answered him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88].

﴿And Dhu al-Nun, when he went off in anger, and thought that We would not decree (any hardship) for him, then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been among the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿So We answered him and saved him from distress, and thus do We save the believers.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 88] That is: remember Dhu al-Nun, meaning the companion of the fish, who is Yunus (peace be upon him), and his patience in what befell him, then his turning back (to God) and his deliverance, so that your heart may be firmly settled regarding his account, and your inner self may be strengthened to endure what the tyrants say. This story is mentioned here, in Surat al-Saffat, and in Surat al-Qalam. The reason is that Yunus ibn Matta (peace be upon him) was commanded by God to go to the people of Nineveh, from the land of Mosul, the seat of the rule of the Assyrians, to call them to faith in Him alone, to the establishment of justice, the spreading of equity, and good conduct. But they were the opposite of this: their disbelief had grown great and their evil had multiplied. He feared that the matter would not be accomplished for him among them, so he fled from Bayt al-Maqdis to Jaffa, and boarded a ship sailing to Tarshish to settle there. God sent a violent wind upon the sea, and the ship was nearly sinking with him aboard. The passengers lightened it of their goods, but this did not help. It came into their minds that there was a person in the ship on account of whom they would perish, so they cast lots to see who it was, and the lot fell upon Yunus. They threw him into the sea, and its turbulence and its waves subsided. God prepared a fish for Yunus, which swallowed him, and he remained in the belly of the fish for three days. Then he called upon his Lord, and He answered him, and the fish cast him onto the shore. Then God revealed to Yunus a second time that he should set out for Nineveh and call its people to God, Exalted is He. He reached it and proclaimed to them the Oneness (of God) and repentance. He warned them that if they did not believe, Nineveh would be overturned with them. When they became certain of this, they believed. So God lifted the punishment from them. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy (their lives) for a time.﴾ [Yunus: 98]

**Notes:**

**First:** Yunus (peace be upon him) is called Yunan in the Torah, and he is Hebrew. It is said that he was from Gath-hepher, a town in the tribe of Zebulun, in the north of the Holy Land. It is also said that he was sent as a prophet about eight hundred years before the Messiah. And God knows best.

**Second:** Most of the exegetes (as al-Razi related) hold that Yunus went off angry at his Lord. They hold that by fleeing to the ship, and by abandoning his journey to Nineveh at first, he thought that he would be left alone and would not be held to account. Some of the scholars of verification said: Yunus only opposed the divine command at first and took a concession regarding it, fearing that he would be thought a false prophet if the people of Nineveh repented and God pardoned their sin. The use of the intensive form in (mughadiban) is for emphasis, because its root implies a relation between two parties, each of whom strives hard to overcome the other. It therefore requires exerting one's utmost power and reaching the extreme, so it is used for its consequence, the intensification, without the sense of (mufa'ala) (reciprocal action) being intended. The apparent meaning of this verse and similar verses has been used as evidence by those who hold that prophets may commit error, except lying in conveying the message, for error in it is not permissible for them, since it is the proof of God over His servants; and except in what pertains to the explanation of revelation, for error is not permissible for them when explaining what is legislated. This is the view of the Karramiyya (a sect) against the Murji'a, as in the commentary on Nahj al-Balagha by Ibn Abi al-Hadid. (The view of al-Baqillani of the Ash'ariyya (as related by Ibn Hazm in al-Milal)): As for the majority who prevent that, they have interpretations for this verse and its like. We prefer what Ibn Hazm said on this matter, because he was more outspoken. He, may God have mercy on him, said, after relating the view of the Karramiyya mentioned above: The Ahl al-Sunna, the Mu'tazila, the Najjariyya, the Kharijites, and the Shi'a hold that it is absolutely impossible for a prophet to commit deliberate disobedience, whether a minor or a major sin.

He then said: This is the view by which we religiously submit to God, Exalted is He, and it is not permissible for anyone to hold any other. We say: Forgetfulness without intent may occur from prophets. They may also intend something seeking the face of God, Exalted is He, and nearness to Him by it, and it may then coincide with what is contrary to God's intended purpose. However, God, Exalted is He, never confirms them in either of these two aspects at all, but rather He will certainly alert them to this after it occurs from them. Sometimes He makes them dislike what is undesirable in this world, as happened to Adam, Yunus, and the (other) prophets (peace be upon them), unlike us in this regard. For we are not held to account for what we forget, nor for what we intend by seeking the face of God, Mighty and Majestic, when it does not coincide with His intended purpose. Rather, we are rewarded for this with one reward.

He then said (in discussing Yunus, peace be upon him): As for God's report that Yunus went off angry, he never became angry at his Lord, nor did God say that he was angry with his Lord. Whoever adds this addition has attributed a lie to God and added to the Qur'an what is not in it. This is not permissible, and it is not allowable to suspect of anyone with even a little measure of intellect that he would be angry with his Lord, Exalted is He. How then could a prophet from among the prophets do such a thing? We therefore know with certainty that he was only angry with his people, and this did not coincide with the intended purpose of God, Mighty and Majestic, so he was punished for it, even though Yunus (peace be upon him) only intended by it the pleasure of God, Mighty and Majestic. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and thought that We would not decree (any hardship) for him﴾, it is not as they imagined, a feeble opinion that is not permissible to attribute even to a weak woman or a weak man, unless one has reached the utmost ignorance. How then could it be attributed to a prophet who is preferred over people in knowledge? It is an absolutely certain impossibility that a prophet should think that God, Exalted is He, who sent him with His religion, is unable to do something, while he sees that a human like himself is able to do it. There is no doubt that whoever attributes this to the Prophet ﷺ, the virtuous one, his anger would intensify if it were attributed to him or to his son. How much more so to Yunus ibn Matta, about whom the Messenger of God ﷺ said: ««Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta»». Thus their assumption is without doubt invalid, and it is established that the meaning of His saying: ﴿and thought that We would not decree (any hardship) for him﴾ is: We would not constrict for him, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿As for when He tests him and restricts his provision﴾ [al-Fajr: 16], that is, constricted for him. Yunus (peace be upon him) thought that God, Exalted is He, would not constrict for him in his anger at his people, since he thought he was doing good by that act. God, Mighty and Majestic, only forbade Muhammad ﷺ from being like the companion of the fish. Yes, God, Mighty and Majestic, forbade him from being angry at his people and commanded him to be patient with their harm and to be lenient with them. As for His saying, Exalted is He, that he deserved blame and reproach, and that had it not been for the blessing with which He overtook him, he would have remained punished in the belly of the fish, this is exactly what we have said, that prophets (peace be upon them) are held to account in this world for what they did, which they thought was good and a means of drawing near to God, Mighty and Majestic, when it did not coincide with the intended purpose of their Lord. In this sense, he acknowledged against himself that he had been among the wrongdoers. Wrongdoing is placing a thing in other than its proper place. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) placed anger in other than its proper place, he acknowledged wrongdoing in that. Not because he intended it while knowing that he had wronged. The words of Ibn Hazm end here.

I say: What opens the door to problems is delving deeply into the words, overdoing their explanation, generating meanings and implications for them, and expanding on their aspects to such an extent that it deadens the brilliance of the composition and the purity of its eloquence. It is well known that the Noble Revelation surpassed all other known styles of speech in its wondrous style. For this reason it is a verse that seizes the hearts with tenderness, harmony, eloquence, and order. You do not find in its words anything but the choicest for their delicacy, nor in its sentences anything but the most majestic in structure, nor in its allusions anything but the strongest in symbolism, nor in its metaphors anything but the highest in meaning. Among this is its practice in blame and warning, of casting speech in the most forceful and emphatic mold, from which the severity of the matter and the strength of the reproach are understood. This is because of the might of the divine presence and the lordly station. Thus the eloquent Arab by nature, who has an innate taste, when the summary account of Yunus (peace be upon him) is recited to him in this verse, is astonished by what it conveys of the strength of reproach and blame, and that by fleeing he angered his master with an anger not comparable to the anger at the disobedient. For the good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near (to God). He thought he would be forgotten and not held to account, and would escape and not be confined, but there came to him what had not been in his mind, and he fell into the snare of the power of the Most High. Then grace overtook him, and mercy reached him. This is the summary of what is understood from the verse, explicitly and implicitly. So understand what I have mentioned to you, for it will bring you as much verification as you hope for.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[89] ﴿And Zechariah, when he called to his Lord: "My Lord, do not leave me alone (without an heir), and You are the best of inheritors."﴾

﴿And Zechariah﴾, i.e., mention his account: ﴿when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone"﴾, i.e., at the time when he asked that his Lord grant him a son who would be a prophet after him, and not leave him alone and solitary without an heir. The story has already been presented at length at the beginning of Surat Maryam and also in Surat Ali 'Imran. As for His saying, ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾, (p-4305) it is a praise appropriate to the request. Al-Ghazali said in (Sharh al-Asma' al-Husna): The Warith (the Inheritor) is the one to whom possessions return after the passing away of their owners. That is God, glory be to Him, for He is the Everlasting after the annihilation of His creation, and to Him is the return of everything and its final destination. His, may He be exalted, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 90:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[90] ﴿So We answered him and gave him Yahya, and We made his wife fit for childbearing for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds, and they would call upon Us in hope and in fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us.﴾

﴿So We answered him﴾, i.e., his supplication. ﴿And We gave him Yahya and made his wife fit for him﴾, i.e., We made her fit for childbearing after her barrenness, as a miracle and an honor for him. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds﴾, it is a reason (ta'lil) for the varieties of His beneficence, exalted is He, related to the prophets mentioned, i.e., they would hasten in every avenue of goodness. The choice of (fi, "in") over (ila, "to") indicates their steadfastness and firm establishment in the essence of goodness, because (ila) denotes departure from a thing and directing oneself toward it. ﴿And they would call upon Us in hope and in fear﴾, i.e., possessors of desire and dread, or desirous of reward and hopeful of being answered. ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾, i.e., humble, supplicating. As for His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[91] ﴿And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾

﴿And she who guarded her chastity﴾ That is: mention the account of she who guarded it with complete guarding, from the lawful and the unlawful alike. As she said: ﴿No man has touched me﴾ [Maryam: 20]. The expression of her by the relative pronoun is to magnify her station and to absolve her of what they alleged concerning her, from the very beginning. ﴿So We breathed into her of Our Spirit﴾ That is: We breathed the Spirit into Jesus within her; that is, We gave him life in her womb. The breathing of the Spirit into Jesus, since he was in Maryam's womb, took the place of breathing the Spirit into her. Breathing the spirit into a body is an expression for giving it life. It was also said that the meaning is: We performed the breathing into her from Our Spirit, Jibril (peace be upon him), that is, We commanded him and he breathed. Or: We breathed into her some of Our Spirit, that is, some of the created spirits belonging to Us; and that portion is the spirit of Jesus, because it reached her through the air that He breathed into her womb. ﴿And We made her and her son﴾ That is, their account ﴿a sign for the worlds﴾ That is: in the perfection of His power and in His singling out whom He wills with what He wills. Among their signs were the provision coming to Maryam out of season, the fruiting of the dry palm tree, the flowing of the spring, the speech of her son in the cradle, the raising of the dead, and the healing of the blind and the leper.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say, why was it not said "two signs," as He said: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾ [al-Isra: 12]? I say: because their condition together is one sign, namely her bearing him without a male. End of quote. It was also said: the meaning is "We made her a sign and her son a sign," so the first was omitted because the second indicates it. When He, exalted is He, had concluded what He mentioned of the affair of a group of the prophets, may the blessings of God be upon them, He pointed out that their creed and the foundations of their religion are one, by His saying, glorified and exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, Exalted is He, saying:

[92] ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.﴾

﴿Indeed, this﴾ means: the cause of monotheism and of submission to one Deity with no partner. ﴿Your community﴾ means: your religion (milla), which you must safeguard its limits and observe its rights. The address is to all people. ﴿One community﴾ means: not divided. Rather, it is one religion, meaning that all the Prophets and Messengers of God are upon one religion and one faith, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the religion with God is Islam﴾ (Al 'Imran: 19). ﴿And I am your Lord﴾ means: there is no god for you other than Me. ﴿So worship Me﴾ means: and do not associate anything with Me.

(p-4307) Note:

We have said that "ummah" here means milla, which is the religion upon which people are gathered, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a ummah﴾ (al-Zukhruf: 22), meaning: upon a religion upon which they are gathered. This meaning of ummah is what many of the exegetes (mufassirun) preferred in this verse and in the verse: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 51), ﴿And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 52). The word "ummah" is also used with the meaning of a group, as in His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿And among those We created is a community that guides by the truth and by it acts justly﴾ (al-A'raf: 181), meaning: a group. And as in His saying: ﴿And let there be among you a community that invites to good, enjoins what is right, and forbids what is wrong﴾ (Al 'Imran: 104). It is not used in the sense of "group" absolutely; rather, it means a group bound by a bond of association, who are regarded as one entity, and it is permissible for them to be given one name, such as the name "ummah." The word "ummah" is also used with the meaning of years, as in His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted ummah﴾ (Hud: 8), and in His saying: ﴿And he remembered after an ummah﴾ (Yusuf: 45). It is also used with the meaning of a leader who is followed, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was an ummah, devoutly obedient to God﴾ (al-Nahl: 120). And it is used with the meaning of one of the known nations, as in His saying: ﴿You are the best ummah brought forth for mankind﴾ (Al 'Imran: 110). This last meaning does not depart from the meaning of "group," as we have mentioned; rather, custom (al-'urf) has specialized it in this sense. This is how the scholar Muhammad Abduh, may God have mercy on him, verified it in his commentary on the verse: ﴿Mankind was one ummah﴾ (al-Baqarah: 213).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 93:

(p-4308) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[93] ﴿And they have divided their affair among themselves into sects; to Us all will they return.﴾

﴿And they have divided their affair among themselves into sects; to Us all will they return.﴾ That is: the people divided in their religion which Allah commanded them with and called them to, so they became factions (ahzab) and sects (milal) within it.

Al-Zamakhshari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The original wording would be (wa-taqatta'tum, "you divided"), but the speech was turned to the third person by way of iltifat (shift of grammatical person). It is as if He is denouncing to others what they have corrupted and disparaging their conduct in their eyes, saying to them: "Do you not see the enormity of what these people have committed in the religion of Allah?" The meaning is that they made the matter of their religion into pieces (qat'an) among themselves, just as a group divides a thing and shares it out, so that one gets a portion and another gets a portion, as a figure of their disagreement about it and their becoming scattered groups and diverse factions. Then He threatened them that these divided sects will return to Him. So He is the one who reckons with them and recompenses them, rewarding the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[94] ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no denial of his effort, and indeed, We record it for him.﴾

﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no denial of his effort, and indeed, We record it for him.﴾ That is: whoever among these people, who have split into factions in their religion, does of the righteous deeds that God has commanded, and obeys Him in His commands and prohibitions, while he affirms the oneness of God, believes in His promise and His threat, and disassociates himself from rivals and false gods, then "there is no denial of his effort." Rather, God gives thanks for this deed of his and rewards him with the reward of the people of obedience. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and indeed, We record it for him﴾, that is, for his effort which is thanked, ﴿We record it﴾, meaning We set it down in the record of his deeds, and We do not waste it.

Note:

Al-kufran (ingratitude, denial) is a verbal noun (masdar) from "Fulan kafara al-ni'mata kufran wa kufranan" (so-and-so was ungrateful for the blessing). The phrasing "la kufrana" (there is no denial) was chosen over "la nakfuru" (we shall not deny) for emphasis (al-mubalagha), because negating the genus (nafy al-jins) entails the negation of the act and is more emphatic in its exoneration (al-tanzih) through its generality. He expressed the deed by "effort" (al-sa'y) to show the esteem given to it. The verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the striving due to it, while he is a believer, those are the ones whose striving will be appreciated﴾ [al-Isra: 19].

Then He pointed to the opposite of these people, namely those who turn away from His remembrance, by the certainty of the threat for them, in accordance with what His custom, exalted is He, has established, in His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[95] ﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed: that they shall not return.﴾

﴿And there is a prohibition upon a town which We have destroyed: that they shall not return.﴾ That is: and it is forbidden for the people of a town who transgressed against the command of their Lord, and whom He destroyed for their sins, that they return to their families. Like His words, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 31] and His words: ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor will they return to their families.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 50] The addition of (lā) here is to emphasise the meaning of negation from (ḥarām), and this is among the wondrous and most eloquent methods of the Revelation, most precise in exactness. The secret of stating the non-return, despite its clarity, is the frank declaration of that which disturbs them, grieves them and wounds them: the everlasting destruction, and the loss of their greatest wish, which is their worldly life.

Abū Muslim made this verse a continuation of what precedes it, and the (lā) in it remains in its proper function. It, together with (ḥarām), is of the type of negating a negation, which indicates affirmation. The meaning: it is forbidden for the destroyed town that it not return to the Hereafter; rather, its return for recompense is obligatory. Thus the purpose is to refute the words of one who denies the Resurrection. The verification of what preceded is that there is no denial of anyone's effort, and that He, glorified is He, will give him life, and recompense him for his deed. The noble wording admits this and becomes clear in it. However, the first (interpretation) is more appropriate for observing the parallels in the verses. As for mentioning other than these two, the context does not indicate it, nor does the parallel; and in it is what impairs eloquence, namely convolution and the loss of smoothness of expression.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verse 96:

Then he pointed to the realization of the victory of the messengers, their triumph, and the abundance of their followers, so that they encircle their enemies from every side and inflict upon them that at which their eyes will stare, leaving them with prolonged regret, by His saying, exalted is He:

(p-4310)The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[96] ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swarm down from every slope.﴾

﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾: "Gog and Magog" is a designation for every numerous nation, intermingled from various kinds of peoples. ﴿And they swarm down from every slope﴾: that is, they rush forth from every elevated place on the earth, mobilizing to subdue their enemies, under the banner of their prophet, their commander, or their caliph.

The Explanation of His Words, exalted is He:

[97] ﴿And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly. "Woe to us! We were certainly heedless of this; nay, we were wrongdoers."﴾

﴿And the true promise draws near﴾ means: the forerunners of victory, domination, and the crushing of falsehood and disbelief have appeared. ﴿Behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾ means: because of the terror that has descended upon them and the bewilderment at it, saying: ﴿"Woe to us! We were certainly heedless of this"﴾, that is, we did not know that it was true. ﴿"Nay, we were wrongdoers"﴾, that is, against ourselves, by neglecting reflection and by their refusal and obstinacy. Then He, glorified is He, pointed to their state in the Hereafter with His words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 21, verses 98–100:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[98] ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; to it you will be brought.﴾ [99] ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it. And all of them will abide therein.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 99] [100] ﴿For them therein is a groaning, and they therein will not hear.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 100].

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., of the idols and images: ﴿are the fuel of Hell﴾, i.e., that which is thrown into it: ﴿to it you will be brought﴾. ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it. And all of them will abide therein﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 99], i.e., there is no escape for them from it.

(p-4311) Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why were they joined with their gods? I say: because they will continue, by being in its company, in increased grief and anguish, since what befell them was on their account, and looking at the face of an enemy is a form of punishment. Also, because they had assumed that they would seek intercession from them in the Hereafter and benefit from their intercession. When they encounter the matter contrary to what they had assumed, nothing will be more hateful to them than them (the gods). ﴿For them therein is a groaning﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 100], i.e., the repeated drawing of breath by which the ribs swell. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 100], i.e., because of the terror and the severity of the punishment.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the condition of the believers after the condition of the disbelievers, in accordance with the customary method of the revelation, which pairs promise with threat and presents encouragement alongside warning, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[101] ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us – those will be kept far away from it.﴾ [102] ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in what their souls desire, forever.﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 102] [103] ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying, "This is your day which you were promised."﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 103].

﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾ means: the excellent attribute (al-khaslah al-husna), which is felicity or divine success (al-tawfiq). ﴿Those will be kept far away from it﴾ because they are in the lofty chambers of the Gardens, secure, since their Lord has protected them from the torment of the Blaze. ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 102], that is, a sound that could be perceived from it, because of their distance from it and from whatever would frighten them. ﴿And they will abide in what their souls desire, forever﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 102]. ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 103], that is, the terror of the Gathering, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And on the Day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾ [An-Naml: 87]. ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 103], that is, they will meet them, congratulating them and saying: ﴿This is your day which you were promised﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 103], that is, in the worldly life, and you are given good news of attaining the excellent reward therein.

وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى:

(p-٤٣١٢) القَوْلُ في تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى:

[١٠٤] ﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ كَما بَدَأْنا أوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وعْدًا عَلَيْنا إنّا كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾ [١٠٥] ﴿ولَقَدْ كَتَبْنا في الزَّبُورِ مِن بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أنَّ الأرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصّالِحُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٥] [١٠٦] ﴿إنَّ في هَذا لَبَلاغًا لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٦] [١٠٧] ﴿وما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٧].

﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ﴾ أي: اذْكُرْه. أو هو ظرفٌ لـ ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٣]، أو لـ "تَتَلَقّاهم". والطَّيُّ ضدُّ النَّشْرِ. وقولُهُ: ﴿كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ﴾ أي: كما يُطْوى السِّجِلُّ، وهو الكتابُ. واللامُ في "لِلْكُتُبِ" لامُ التَّبيين. ولذلك قُرئ: "الكِتابِ" بالإفراد. أو بمعنى "مِن"، وفيه قربٌ من الأول. أو "الكُتُبِ" بمعنى المَكْتُوب، أي: كطيِّ الصحيفةِ على مكتوبِها، فاللامُ بمعنى "على"، وهو ما اختاره ابنُ جَرير.

تَنْبِيهٌ:

ما نُقل عن ابنِ عباسٍ أنَّ "السِّجِلَّ" اسمُ رجلٍ كان يكتبُ للنبيِّ (ﷺ)، كما رواه أبو داود والنسائيُّ وغيرُهما، فأثرٌ مُنكَرٌ لا يصحّ.

قال ابنُ كثير: وقد صرّح بوضعِه جماعةٌ من الحُفّاظ، وإنْ كان في سُنَنِ أبي داود، منهم شيخُنا الحافظُ أبو الحَجّاجِ المِزِّيُّ.

وكذلك تقدّم في ردِّه الإمامُ ابنُ جَرير وقال: لا يُعرَفُ في الصحابةِ أحدٌ اسمُه "السِّجِلُّ". (p-٤٣١٣) وكتّابُ النبيِّ (ﷺ) معروفون، وليس فيهم أحدٌ اسمُه "السِّجِلُّ".

وصدق رحمه الله في ذلك، وهو من أقوى الأدلةِ على نكارةِ هذا الحديث.

وأما من ذكره في أسماءِ الصحابة، فإنما اعتمد على هذا الحديث. والصحيحُ عن ابنِ عباسٍ أنَّ "السِّجِلَّ" هي الصحيفةُ. انتهى.

هذه الآيةُ كآيةِ: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [الزمر: ٦٧]. وطيُّ السماءِ كنايةٌ عن انكدارِ نجومِها، ومحوِ رسومِها، بفسادِ تركيبِها واختلالِ نظامِها، فلا يبقى أمرُ ما فيها من الكواكبِ على ما نراه اليوم، فيُخَرَّبُ العالَمُ بأسرِه: ﴿كَما بَدَأْنا أوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وعْدًا عَلَيْنا إنّا كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾، أي: مُنجِزِينَ إيّاه. ثم أشار إلى تحقيقِ مِصداقِه، بإعزازِ المُنبِئِ عنه، وإيراثِه مُلكَ جاحدِه، بقولِه تعالى: ﴿ولَقَدْ كَتَبْنا في الزَّبُورِ مِن بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أنَّ الأرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصّالِحُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٥]، أي: العاملون بطاعتِه، المنتهون إلى أمرِه ونهيِه، دونَ العاملين منهم بمعصيتِه، المؤثِرين طاعةَ الشيطانِ على طاعتِه. و"الزَّبُورُ" عَلَمٌ على كتابِ داودَ عليه السلام، ويُقال: المرادُ به كلُّ كتابٍ مُنَزَّلٍ. و"الذِّكْرُ"، قالوا: التوراةُ، أو أمُّ الكتاب، يعني اللوحَ الذي كُتب فيه كلُّ شيءٍ قبل الخلق، والله أعلم.

وقولُه تعالى: ﴿إنَّ في هَذا لَبَلاغًا لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٦] إشارةٌ إلى المذكورِ في هذه السورةِ من الأخبارِ والوعدِ والوعيدِ والمواعظِ البالغة، أو إلى العِبرةِ في إيراثِ الأرضِ الصالحين ودَحرِ المجرمين. و"البَلاغُ" الكفايةُ. وقولُه: ﴿لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٦] أي: يعبدونَ اللهَ بما شَرَعه وأحبَّه ورَضِيه، ويُؤثِرونَ طاعتَه على طاعةِ الشياطينِ وشهواتِ النفسِ.

﴿وما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٧] أي: وما أرسلناك بهذه الحنيفيةِ والدينِ الفِطريِّ إلا حالَ كونِكَ رحمةً للخلق، فإنَّ ما بُعثتَ به سببٌ لسعادةِ الدارين. وفي جعلِه نفسَ الرحمةِ مبالغةٌ جليّة. وجُوِّز كونُ "رَحْمَةً" مفعولًا له، أي: لِلرحمة، فهو نبيُّ الرحمة.

(p-٤٣١٤) تَنْبِيهٌ:

قال الرازيُّ: إنه عليه السلام كان رحمةً في الدينِ وفي الدنيا. أما في الدينِ فلأنه بُعث والناسُ في جاهليةٍ وضلالة، وأهلُ الكتابين كانوا في حيرةٍ من أمرِ دينِهم لطولِ مُكثِهم، وانقطاعِ تواتُرِهم، ووقوعِ الاختلافِ في كتبِهم. فبعثَ اللهُ تعالى محمدًا (ﷺ) حين لم يكنْ لطالبِ الحقِّ سبيلٌ إلى الفوزِ والثوابِ، فدعاهم إلى الحقِّ، وبيَّن لهم سبيلَ الثواب، وشرع لهم الأحكام، وميّز الحلالَ من الحرام. ثم إنما ينتفعُ بهذه الرحمةِ من كانت همّتُه طلبَ الحق، فلا يركنُ إلى التقليدِ ولا إلى العنادِ والاستكبار، وكان التوفيقُ قرينًا له. قال اللهُ تعالى: ﴿قُلْ هو لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وشِفاءٌ﴾ [فصلت: ٤٤] إلى قولِه تعالى: ﴿وهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾ [فصلت: ٤٤]. وأما في الدنيا فلأنهم تخلّصوا بسببه من كثيرٍ من الذلِّ والقتالِ والحروب، ونُصروا ببركةِ دينِه. انتهى.

وقد أشرتُ إلى وجهِ الرحمةِ في بعثتِه (ﷺ) في "الشَّذْرَةِ" التي جمعتُها في سيرتِه الزكية، في بيانِ افتقارِ الناسِ جميعًا إلى رسالتِه، فقلتُ: كلُّ من لحَظ بعينِ الحكمةِ والاعتبار، ونَفَذَتْ بصيرتُه إلى مكنونِ الأسرار، علِمَ حاجةَ البشرِ كافةً إلى رسالةِ خاتمِ النبيين، وأكبرَ منّةَ اللهِ به على العالَمين. فقد بُعث صلواتُ اللهِ عليه وسلامُه على حينِ فترةٍ من الرسل، وإخافةٍ للسُّبل، وانتشارٍ من الأهواء، وتفرقٍ من الملل، ما بين مُشبِّهٍ لله بخلقِه، ومُلحدٍ في اسمِه، ومُشيرٍ إلى غيرِه: كفرٌ بَواحٌ، وشركٌ صُراحٌ، وفسادٌ عامّ، وانتهابٌ للأموالِ والأرواح، واغتصابٌ للحقوق، وشنٌّ للغارات، ووأدٌ للبنات، وأكلٌ للدماءِ والميتات، وقطعٌ للأرحام، وإعلانٌ بالسِّفاح، وتحريفٌ للكتبِ المنزلة، واعتقادٌ لأضاليلِ المتكهنة، وتأليهٌ للأحبارِ والرهبان، وسيطرةٌ من جبابرةِ الجورِ وزعماءِ الفتنِ وقادةِ الغرور، ظلماتٌ بعضُها فوقَ بعض، وطامّاتٌ طبّقت أكنافَ الأرض، استمرّت الأممُ على هذه الحال، الأجيالَ الطوال، حتى دعا داعي الفلاحِ، وأذِن اللهُ تعالى بالإصلاح. فأحدثَ بعدَ ذلك أمرًا، وجعلَ بعدَ عسرٍ يسرًا، فإنَّ النوائبَ إذا تناهت انتهت، وإذا توالت تولّت. وذلك أنَّ اللهَ تعالى أرسلَ إلى البشرِ رسولًا ليُعتقهم من أسرِ الأوثان، (p-٤٣١٥) ويُخرجَهم من ظلمةِ الكفرِ وعَمى التقليدِ إلى نورِ الإيمان، ويُنقذَهم من النارِ والعار، ويرفعَ عنهم الآصار، ويُطهّرَهم من مساوئِ الأخلاقِ والأعمال، ويُرشدَهم إلى صراطِ الحق. قال تعالى: ﴿وما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٧]. وقال تعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولا مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ ويُزَكِّيهِمْ ويُعَلِّمُهُمُ الكِتابَ والحِكْمَةَ وإنْ كانُوا مِن قَبْلُ لَفي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٦٤]. انتهى.

﴿يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ﴾ أي: اذْكُرْه. أو هو ظرفٌ لـ ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٣]، أو لـ "تَتَلَقّاهم". والطَّيُّ ضدُّ النَّشْرِ. وقولُهُ: ﴿كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ﴾ أي: كما يُطْوى السِّجِلُّ، وهو الكتابُ. واللامُ في "لِلْكُتُبِ" لامُ التَّبيين. ولذلك قُرئ: "الكِتابِ" بالإفراد. أو بمعنى "مِن"، وفيه قربٌ من الأول. أو "الكُتُبِ" بمعنى المَكْتُوب، أي: كطيِّ الصحيفةِ على مكتوبِها، فاللامُ بمعنى "على"، وهو ما اختاره ابنُ جَرير.

تَنْبِيهٌ:

ما نُقل عن ابنِ عباسٍ أنَّ "السِّجِلَّ" اسمُ رجلٍ كان يكتبُ للنبيِّ (ﷺ)، كما رواه أبو داود والنسائيُّ وغيرُهما، فأثرٌ مُنكَرٌ لا يصحّ.

قال ابنُ كثير: وقد صرّح بوضعِه جماعةٌ من الحُفّاظ، وإنْ كان في سُنَنِ أبي داود، منهم شيخُنا الحافظُ أبو الحَجّاجِ المِزِّيُّ.

وكذلك تقدّم في ردِّه الإمامُ ابنُ جَرير وقال: لا يُعرَفُ في الصحابةِ أحدٌ اسمُه "السِّجِلُّ". (p-٤٣١٣) وكتّابُ النبيِّ (ﷺ) معروفون، وليس فيهم أحدٌ اسمُه "السِّجِلُّ".

وصدق رحمه الله في ذلك، وهو من أقوى الأدلةِ على نكارةِ هذا الحديث.

وأما من ذكره في أسماءِ الصحابة، فإنما اعتمد على هذا الحديث. والصحيحُ عن ابنِ عباسٍ أنَّ "السِّجِلَّ" هي الصحيفةُ. انتهى.

هذه الآيةُ كآيةِ: ﴿وما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [الزمر: ٦٧]. وطيُّ السماءِ كنايةٌ عن انكدارِ نجومِها، ومحوِ رسومِها، بفسادِ تركيبِها واختلالِ نظامِها، فلا يبقى أمرُ ما فيها من الكواكبِ على ما نراه اليوم، فيُخَرَّبُ العالَمُ بأسرِه: ﴿كَما بَدَأْنا أوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وعْدًا عَلَيْنا إنّا كُنّا فاعِلِينَ﴾، أي: مُنجِزِينَ إيّاه. ثم أشار إلى تحقيقِ مِصداقِه، بإعزازِ المُنبِئِ عنه، وإيراثِه مُلكَ جاحدِه، بقولِه تعالى: ﴿ولَقَدْ كَتَبْنا في الزَّبُورِ مِن بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ أنَّ الأرْضَ يَرِثُها عِبادِيَ الصّالِحُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٥]، أي: العاملون بطاعتِه، المنتهون إلى أمرِه ونهيِه، دونَ العاملين منهم بمعصيتِه، المؤثِرين طاعةَ الشيطانِ على طاعتِه. و"الزَّبُورُ" عَلَمٌ على كتابِ داودَ عليه السلام، ويُقال: المرادُ به كلُّ كتابٍ مُنَزَّلٍ. و"الذِّكْرُ"، قالوا: التوراةُ، أو أمُّ الكتاب، يعني اللوحَ الذي كُتب فيه كلُّ شيءٍ قبل الخلق، والله أعلم.

وقولُه تعالى: ﴿إنَّ في هَذا لَبَلاغًا لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٦] إشارةٌ إلى المذكورِ في هذه السورةِ من الأخبارِ والوعدِ والوعيدِ والمواعظِ البالغة، أو إلى العِبرةِ في إيراثِ الأرضِ الصالحين ودَحرِ المجرمين. و"البَلاغُ" الكفايةُ. وقولُه: ﴿لِقَوْمٍ عابِدِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٦] أي: يعبدونَ اللهَ بما شَرَعه وأحبَّه ورَضِيه، ويُؤثِرونَ طاعتَه على طاعةِ الشياطينِ وشهواتِ النفسِ.

قال الرازيُّ: إنه عليه السلام كان رحمةً في الدينِ وفي الدنيا. أما في الدينِ فلأنه بُعث والناسُ في جاهليةٍ وضلالة، وأهلُ الكتابين كانوا في حيرةٍ من أمرِ دينِهم لطولِ مُكثِهم، وانقطاعِ تواتُرِهم، ووقوعِ الاختلافِ في كتبِهم. فبعثَ اللهُ تعالى محمدًا (ﷺ) حين لم يكنْ لطالبِ الحقِّ سبيلٌ إلى الفوزِ والثوابِ، فدعاهم إلى الحقِّ، وبيَّن لهم سبيلَ الثواب، وشرع لهم الأحكام، وميّز الحلالَ من الحرام. ثم إنما ينتفعُ بهذه الرحمةِ من كانت همّتُه طلبَ الحق، فلا يركنُ إلى التقليدِ ولا إلى العنادِ والاستكبار، وكان التوفيقُ قرينًا له. قال اللهُ تعالى: ﴿قُلْ هو لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وشِفاءٌ﴾ [فصلت: ٤٤] إلى قولِه تعالى: ﴿وهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾ [فصلت: ٤٤]. وأما في الدنيا فلأنهم تخلّصوا بسببه من كثيرٍ من الذلِّ والقتالِ والحروب، ونُصروا ببركةِ دينِه. انتهى.

وقد أشرتُ إلى وجهِ الرحمةِ في بعثتِه (ﷺ) في "الشَّذْرَةِ" التي جمعتُها في سيرتِه الزكية، في بيانِ افتقارِ الناسِ جميعًا إلى رسالتِه، فقلتُ: كلُّ من لحَظ بعينِ الحكمةِ والاعتبار، ونَفَذَتْ بصيرتُه إلى مكنونِ الأسرار، علِمَ حاجةَ البشرِ كافةً إلى رسالةِ خاتمِ النبيين، وأكبرَ منّةَ اللهِ به على العالَمين. فقد بُعث صلواتُ اللهِ عليه وسلامُه على حينِ فترةٍ من الرسل، وإخافةٍ للسُّبل، وانتشارٍ من الأهواء، وتفرقٍ من الملل، ما بين مُشبِّهٍ لله بخلقِه، ومُلحدٍ في اسمِه، ومُشيرٍ إلى غيرِه: كفرٌ بَواحٌ، وشركٌ صُراحٌ، وفسادٌ عامّ، وانتهابٌ للأموالِ والأرواح، واغتصابٌ للحقوق، وشنٌّ للغارات، ووأدٌ للبنات، وأكلٌ للدماءِ والميتات، وقطعٌ للأرحام، وإعلانٌ بالسِّفاح، وتحريفٌ للكتبِ المنزلة، واعتقادٌ لأضاليلِ المتكهنة، وتأليهٌ للأحبارِ والرهبان، وسيطرةٌ من جبابرةِ الجورِ وزعماءِ الفتنِ وقادةِ الغرور، ظلماتٌ بعضُها فوقَ بعض، وطامّاتٌ طبّقت أكنافَ الأرض، استمرّت الأممُ على هذه الحال، الأجيالَ الطوال، حتى دعا داعي الفلاحِ، وأذِن اللهُ تعالى بالإصلاح. فأحدثَ بعدَ ذلك أمرًا، وجعلَ بعدَ عسرٍ يسرًا، فإنَّ النوائبَ إذا تناهت انتهت، وإذا توالت تولّت. وذلك أنَّ اللهَ تعالى أرسلَ إلى البشرِ رسولًا ليُعتقهم من أسرِ الأوثان، (p-٤٣١٥) ويُخرجَهم من ظلمةِ الكفرِ وعَمى التقليدِ إلى نورِ الإيمان، ويُنقذَهم من النارِ والعار، ويرفعَ عنهم الآصار، ويُطهّرَهم من مساوئِ الأخلاقِ والأعمال، ويُرشدَهم إلى صراطِ الحق. قال تعالى: ﴿وما أرْسَلْناكَ إلا رَحْمَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ١٠٧]. وقال تعالى: ﴿لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولا مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ ويُزَكِّيهِمْ ويُعَلِّمُهُمُ الكِتابَ والحِكْمَةَ وإنْ كانُوا مِن قَبْلُ لَفي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٦٤]. انتهى.

وقَوْلُهُ تَعالى:

The commentary on His words, the Exalted:

[108] ﴿Say: "What is revealed to me is only that your God is one God. Will you then submit?"﴾ [109] ﴿But if they turn away, say: "I have announced to you on equal terms, and I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far."﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109] [110] ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 110] [111] ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 111] [112] ﴿He said: "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe."﴾ [al-Anbiya: 112].

﴿Say: "What is revealed to me is only that your God is one God."﴾ That is: what is revealed to me is nothing but that He, the Exalted, alone possesses oneness in divinity. The meaning of the restriction (al-qasr, a grammatical device restricting a predicate to a subject) here is that He is the original and fundamental principle, and everything else returns to Him as a subordinate part. It is a restriction of address (qasr du'a'i): ﴿Will you then submit?﴾ That is: will you yield to and be obedient to what is revealed of monotheism, and surrender to it?

﴿But if they turn away﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is, from monotheism, ﴿say: "I have announced to you on equal terms"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is: I have informed you and guided you to a word that is equal between us and you, by which we believe and reap the fruits of its happiness in both abodes. Or the meaning is: I have pointed you to the straight path, and I have conveyed the matter to you concerning it. If you believe in it, you have attained happiness; otherwise, the promise of the deniers will certainly come upon you, and it will not be turned away from you. And although I do not know when that will be, because God, the Exalted, has not informed me of His knowledge of it and has not made me aware of it, as He said: ﴿And I do not know﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is: I do not know ﴿whether it is near or far, what you are promised﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is: of victory over you, the inheritance of your land by others, and the descent of humiliation and disgrace upon you because of your disobedience. ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya: 110], that is: so He will requite you for that. ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ [al-Anbiya: 111], that is: I do not know, perhaps the delay of your recompense is a gradual leading toward ruin (istidraj) for you and an increase in your being led astray, or a test to see how you will act. So "trial" (al-fitnah) is either a metaphor for istidraj, by mentioning the cause and intending the effect, or it retains its original meaning. In that case it is an explicit metaphor (isti'arah musarrahah). His words, the Exalted: ﴿and an enjoyment for a time﴾ [al-Anbiya: 111], that is: a granting of enjoyment to you until a determined term. Al-tamtie (enjoyment) means preservation and delay. He said, and it was read: "Say: My Lord, judge with truth", that is: decide between us and them with truth. This means granting victory to the one who believed in what You sent down over the one who disbelieved in it, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders﴾ [al-A'raf: 89]. ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya: 112], that is: against the lies and fabrications against God and His Messenger, by granting victory to His allies and subduing His enemies. He, glory be to Him, has answered his supplication and made His word manifest, so to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, indeed He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.

Al-Razi said: Al-Qadi said: God concluded this surah with His words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, judge with truth"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 112] because he, peace be upon him, had gone to the utmost limit in explaining to them, and they had reached the utmost limit in harming him and denying him. So the most that God commanded him with this was as consolation for him and an indication that the aim was their benefit. When they insist on persisting in their disbelief, then you must turn to your Lord, that He may judge between you and them with truth, either by hastening punishment through jihad or otherwise, or by delaying that. For their affair, even if delayed, is what is bound to happen, and is near. What is reported, that he, peace be upon him, used to say this in his wars, serves as an indication that God commanded him to say this statement, as an urging for the command to strive against them. And success is from God.

And although I do not know when that will be, because God, the Exalted, has not informed me of His knowledge of it and has not made me aware of it, as He said: ﴿And I do not know﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is: I do not know ﴿whether it is near or far, what you are promised﴾ [al-Anbiya: 109], that is: of victory over you, the inheritance of your land by others, and the descent of humiliation and disgrace upon you because of your disobedience. ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾ [al-Anbiya: 110], that is: so He will requite you for that. ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you﴾ [al-Anbiya: 111], that is: I do not know, perhaps the delay of your recompense is a gradual leading toward ruin (istidraj) for you and an increase in your being led astray, or a test to see how you will act. So "trial" (al-fitnah) is either a metaphor for istidraj, by mentioning the cause and intending the effect, or it retains its original meaning. In that case it is an explicit metaphor (isti'arah musarrahah). His words, the Exalted: ﴿and an enjoyment for a time﴾ [al-Anbiya: 111], that is: a granting of enjoyment to you until a determined term. Al-tamtie (enjoyment) means preservation and delay. He said, and it was read: "Say: My Lord, judge with truth", that is: decide between us and them with truth. This means granting victory to the one who believed in what You sent down over the one who disbelieved in it, as in His words, the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders﴾ [al-A'raf: 89]. ﴿And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya: 112], that is: against the lies and fabrications against God and His Messenger, by granting victory to His allies and subduing His enemies. He, glory be to Him, has answered his supplication and made His word manifest, so to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, indeed He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.

Al-Razi said: Al-Qadi said: God concluded this surah with His words: ﴿He said: "My Lord, judge with truth"﴾ [al-Anbiya: 112] because he, peace be upon him, had gone to the utmost limit in explaining to them, and they had reached the utmost limit in harming him and denying him. So the most that God commanded him with this was as consolation for him and an indication that the aim was their benefit. When they insist on persisting in their disbelief, then you must turn to your Lord, that He may judge between you and them with truth, either by hastening punishment through jihad or otherwise, or by delaying that. For their affair, even if delayed, is what is bound to happen, and is near. What is reported, that he, peace be upon him, used to say this in his wars, serves as an indication that God commanded him to say this statement, as an urging for the command to strive against them. And success is from God.
